newsitem.title: SPAIN: Tourists drown in Spain after ignoring warnings.
newsitem.headline: Tourists drown in Spain after ignoring warnings.

text.p: One French and one German tourist drowned and 80 people had to be rescued off Spain's northeastern coast after bathers refused to heed lifeguards' warnings to keep out of stormy seas, officials said on Thursday.

Red Cross officials said tourists, mostly from France and Germany, ignored red-flag warnings of strong currents on Wednesday on a popular Costa Brava beach. Some confronted lifeguards who tried to stop them going into the water.
"They even surrounded one of the lifeguards and threatened to hit him," local Red Cross chief Eduard Puig told reporters.
Lifeguards had to call in police reinforcements to rescue people at the Sant Pere Pescador beach near the Catalonian city of Girona.
Rescuers put out in boats to pull bathers from the sea.
The two tourists who died were identified by Spanish news reports as a 48-year-old German man and a 72-year-old Frenchman. Red Cross officials declined to give their names.
